title: Opening a valid link rewrites the address bar with replaceState before the reader acts (T10, T11, and T1, T4, T5, T6, T15, T16)
location: site/src/components/board/ToolFrame.svelte:99-110 (registerInstance takes the toolState of the moment as initial, then every later change goes through stateChanged); site/src/components/tools/T10GeometryStudio.svelte:535-550 (the link is applied in a task after hydration); site/src/components/tools/T11FoldingBench.svelte:221-235
claim: ToolFrame registers the instance before the tool has applied its link. The link's state then reaches history.ts through stateChanged as if the reader had changed it, so 500 ms after load the bar is rewritten, normalised, and on lesson pages written for an instance the reader never touched.
expected: Plan, P1-A2 instruction 5.6: 'Nothing is written on load or hydration; the address bar changes only after the reader acts.' Its fragment decisions/P1-A2.md: 'initial the state shown now; registering writes nothing'. SPEC 7.4: replaceState 'after a move'. SPEC 6.6: 'only instances the reader has changed are written'.
observed: With no action, one replaceState about 0.7 to 1.5 s after load. /tools/geometry/?r=1.0.0 becomes ?z=1&g=A3&r=1.0.0&j=xyz:1,2,3@20,30,0&e=p. /tools/geometry/?j=xyz:1,2,3@370,0,0 becomes ...j=xyz:1,2,3@10,0,0... /tools/fold/?g=A5 becomes ?z=1&g=A5&v=n&c=n&s=1,1,1,1,1&w=&y=5.4.3.2.1. /modules/m7-geometry/?b1.r=0.1 becomes ?b1.z=1&b1.g=A2&b1.r=0.1&b1.j=coxeter&b1.e=p. The same happens on /tools/board/, /tools/lab/, /tools/affine/, /tools/sandbox/, /tools/numbers/ and /tools/mirror/. It does not happen on /tools/garden/, /tools/kostant/, /tools/form/, /tools/symbolic/ or /tools/weyl/, which apply the link before registering. Combined with P4-RT-04-01, this write puts '@NaN' into the bar of a reader who only opened a link.
reproduction: From a clean checkout of b9b8504 plus commit c365fa0: npm ci --prefer-offline; npm run build; PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=<browsers> npx playwright test -c redteam/RT-04/playwright.p4.config.ts redteam-RT-04-p4-findings.spec.ts -g 'finding 3' (10 failing; each prints the replaceState call and the new bar).
specRef: build-plan/agents/P1-A2-site-infra.md 5.6 ('Nothing is written on load or hydration') (plan); decisions/P1-A2.md registerInstance entry; SPEC.md 7.4 History API; SPEC.md 6.6 'only instances the reader has changed are written'; RT-04 attack 21
proposedFix: Let a tool that applies a link after hydration record it without a write: register with the link's state as initial, or add a history.ts call that sets the recorded state and its defaults comparison without scheduling replaceState. Extend history.test.ts 'nothing is written on load' to a link.

refute.citation: SPEC.md 7.4 History API: 'After a move the address bar is updated with replaceState, half a second after the last move of a burst'. SPEC.md 6.6: 'only instances the reader has changed are written'. build-plan/agents/P1-A2-site-infra.md 5.6 (line 173): 'Nothing is written on load or hydration; the address bar changes only after the reader acts.' decisions/P1-A2.md 'History API'. None of these permits a write on load.
refute.evidence: Read at b9b8504 (clean detached worktree). (1) ToolFrame.svelte:99-110 calls registerInstance(id, defaults ?? toolState, ..., toolState) once at hydration, and every later change of toolState goes to stateChanged. (2) history.ts:68-78: stateChanged schedules one replaceState whenever encodeState(state) differs from the recorded state. (3) T10GeometryStudio.svelte:535-550 decodes window.location.search in nextTask after hydration and calls applyLink. The link's state therefore reaches stateChanged as a change, and a write follows about 500 ms later. (4) Records: P1-A2 says '`initial` the state shown now; registering writes nothing'. That record covers registration only, not a link applied after registration. The plan forbids any write on load or hydration (line 173 and checklist line 278). P4-A3 'repair, wave 4.3' records only the scheduling ('A link is read one task after hydration') and nothing about the address bar. P4-A2 records the j normalisation (370 written as 10), which this write makes visible but does not cause. (5) 7.4 has no [D] mark (the heading of 7.6 does). No section 10 default concerns history. (6) History is phase 1 and the tools named are phases 1 to 4, all within G4. gate-G4.md has no item on it. A grep of round1-confirmed-A.json, round1-confirmed-B.json, round1-deferred.json and RESULTS.md for replaceState and 'on load' finds no such finding.
refute.reason: not refuted: R1 failed because 7.4 ties replaceState to moves and 6.6 to instances the reader changed, and nothing permits normalising the bar on load. R2 failed because the finding quotes 7.4, 6.6 and the P1-A2 plan line correctly, and the P1-A2 record ('registering writes nothing') does not cover a link applied after registration. R3 failed because every part is within phases 1 to 4. R4 does not apply, since no oracle function covers history. R5 failed because no [D] passage or recorded decision allows the write. R6 failed because there is no record. Severity none: SPEC 7.4 says when the bar is written but does not in words forbid a write on load; that prohibition is the plan's (P1-A2 5.6), so the rubric does not clearly name this major or minor.

title: KaTeX fonts (font-display: block, not preloaded) arrive after the first paint: a lesson reloaded mid-page shifts by CLS 0.30 to 0.33, and the whole-document relayout adds about 40 percent of M7's TBT
location: site/src/layouts/Lesson.astro and the shared head (no preload of the KaTeX woff2 files); /katex/0.16.47/katex.min.css (20 @font-face rules with font-display:block). The fonts are requested only during the first style and layout of the document.
claim: The KaTeX fonts are discovered late. When they replace the fallback after the first paint, the mathematics in view is laid out again: content in view shifts at a restored reading position, and the whole document is laid out and painted again after FCP.
expected: SPEC 7.6: Cumulative Layout Shift at most 0.1 and Total Blocking Time at most 200 ms on the G4 routes M6 and M7 (360 by 800, 4x). The lens's attack 19 names 'text reflowing when the KaTeX web fonts replace the fallback'.
observed: Reload with the restored scroll position and no input, 4x. M6 y=8178: CLS 0.3334 (2 of 2 runs, one shift at 1170 to 1265 ms, just after FCP at 1032 to 1072 ms; fonts finished 947 to 967 ms). M6 y=14891: 0.3044 (2 of 2). M7 y=19000: 0.3037. M2 y=8000: 0.3015. M7 y=0: 0.0770. With the KaTeX fonts blocked, M6: 0.0000 at both positions. In a copy of M7 that preloads its three fonts (Main-Regular, Math-Italic, SansSerif-Regular): 0.0000 at y=0 and y=19000 (fonts at 115 to 154 ms instead of about 1700 ms). Effect on TBT, from traces of M7 load with Lighthouse categories (3 runs): after FCP the font arrival re-lays out the 37079-px document (Layout 62 to 158 ms) and repaints it (PrePaint and Paint 89 to 134 ms). Alternated observer runs on M7 (5 each, load 1.2 to 1.5): TBT median 319 ms as built against 199 ms with the three preloads. Lighthouse's load at the top reports CLS 0.0000 on M7 and 0.0003 on M6, so the lab run does not see the shift.
reproduction: npm ci --prefer-offline; npm run build; PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-mutation-game/03d88ee7-3b55-5f84-9822-84f78aad9733/scratchpad/pw-browsers node redteam/redteam-RT-07-font-swap-shift.mjs site/dist 5000 /modules/m6-multiple-edges/ 8178,14891 2 (exits 1). Control: BLOCK_FONTS=1 with the same command gives CLS 0. Counterfactual: node redteam/rt07-variant.mjs site/dist /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-mutation-game/03d88ee7-3b55-5f84-9822-84f78aad9733/scratchpad/rt-07-p4/dist-preload /modules/m7-geometry/ preload-fonts, then the font-swap script on that directory with /modules/m7-geometry/ 0,19000 2, and redteam/rt07-load-profile.mjs <dir> /modules/m7-geometry/ 5000 5 <out.json> --cats none on both directories for TBT.
specRef: SPEC.md 7.6 'Lab timings' (CLS at most 0.1; TBT at most 200 ms); 9.1 G4 'lab timings on M6 and M7'
proposedFix: Add <link rel="preload" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin> to each page for the KaTeX fonts it uses. The build knows these from the katex classes in its HTML. The self-hosted KaTeX CSS stays at the installed version.

The reproducer (522fae9:redteam/redteam-RT-07-font-swap-shift.mjs, read as text) loads the page, scrolls with window.scrollTo, then reloads. That scenario is outside the measurement 7.6 and P3-A7 define. The reserved-box sentence covers hydration, not font loading. font-display:block is in KaTeX 0.16.47's own stylesheet, which 7.2 item 2 and CLAUDE.md require to be shipped from the installed version (P0-A3: 'the stylesheet and fonts are copied from that package'). No KaTeX decision in P0-A3, P1-A2 or P0-A5 addresses preloading. TBT half: DECISIONS.md 'P3-X1: other load work looked at (c)' records 'no repeated layout from late fonts was large in the traces, so no preload was added'. That was measured on M0 to M3 before M6 and M7 existed. MERGE P3 stage 3.3 kept the render hint and named the first tool's hydration as what remains. The owner's acceptance ('OWNER: gate G3's lab item accepted as machine-bound') covers G3 on M0 to M5 only. gate-G4.md is RED on M7's TBT (381.3 ms), puts it down to 'likely hydration' and sends it to this round. The known-and-decided list says 'M7's number ... is' still open. The cause the finding names (font relayout after FCP adding about 120 ms on M7) is therefore not recorded or accepted. A builder's no-preload record cannot cover a TBT over the 200 ms of the [D] text.
refute.reason: not refuted: the cause, late KaTeX fonts relaid out after FCP, stands for M7's Total Blocking Time over 200 ms at G4, which no record accepts (owner's acceptance limited to G3 M0 to M5; gate-G4 sends M7 to this round; P3-X1's no-preload record predates M7 and cannot cover a departure from 7.6). Part note: the CLS half (0.30 to 0.33 on a reload at a restored scroll position) is not a violation of 7.6, because 7.6's CLS line is a lab timing, recorded by P3-A7 as Lighthouse's navigation of the route, where M6 and M7 measure 0.0003 and 0.0000 (R2 and R5 hold for that half only). R1 no permitting clause for TBT; R3 M7 is phase 4; R4 not an oracle quantity; R6 gate-G4 records the symptom with a different presumed cause. Major matches the rubric for the TBT half: a stated threshold is exceeded at a gate that requires it.

refute.citation: SPEC.md 7.9 [D; open decision in section 10]: 'A credits page lists every third-party asset with title, author, source and licence, and the licences of bundled libraries and fonts.' 7.3: 'about and credits (phase 0, extended at each release)'. The sentence supports the finding's expected.
refute.evidence: The lockfile at b9b8504 lists clsx 2.1.1 (MIT) as a dependency of svelte 5.57.2 ("clsx": "^2.1.1"). No package.json names it. decisions/P0-A5.md 'the credits list is generated at build time' takes rows only from the dependencies and devDependencies of the three package.json files. RT-FIX-P3-pages added nanostores only. The regression site/tests/unit/dependencies-shipped.test.ts (// regression: P3-RT-08-10) checks only the nanostores row. The MERGE entry 'dependency records completed' attributes the client chunk to svelte and records no licence for clsx. The [D] on 7.9 covers how the page is built, but leaving out a bundled library's licence departs from the [D] text. On R3: 9.1 row 6 lists 'credits, licences', but 7.3 creates the page in phase 0 and extends it at each release. Release 0.5 (G3) has already happened, and round 1 confirmed P3-RT-08-10 on this same page at phase 3. The bundle content itself is for the reproducer to show.
refute.reason: not refuted: R1 7.9 asks for the licences of bundled libraries and nothing excludes transitive ones. R2 the finding quotes 7.9 correctly. R3 the credits page is phase 0, extended at each release, and release 0.5 has passed. R4 not an oracle matter. R5 the P0-A5 package.json rule departs from the [D] text rather than lying within it. R6 the P3-RT-08-10 regression covers nanostores only.
